_meta.notes: Active tab, one sub-tab per CrewStanding present: five hired kerbals spanning every stock standing plus a real RP-1 retiree, and Bill standing down for post-flight R&R. Each row shows name/role/courage/stupidity/rank/experience-toward-next-rank via the shared crew-stat row; Bob Kerman (L5) is at max rank, so his chip reads MAX instead of a redundant 100%. GUS IS THE ROW THAT MATTERS, and this fixture used to get him wrong: it gave him no situationOrdinal at all, with a note saying a mod status has no stock ordinal. RP-1 appends no RosterStatus. It writes stock's Dead, ordinal 2, and remembers the retiree in a private set of its own, which is why every RP-1 retiree used to reach the Dead tab wearing a red fatality badge. So he carries KSP's Dead ordinal AND a Retired standing attributed to the backend that corrected it, which is exactly what the wire carries on a live RP-1 career. Every row carries `standing` because the producer stamps it on every crew entry; the roster-status fallback for an older mod build is exercised by the unit tests, not here.
